explanation.title: Batch the edit. Keep the checks.

paragraphs.text: With atomic patches available from the first turn, Astra combined the imports, root handling and new API/CLI into one patch. It completed in six model requests, down from ten in the first factory round, and passed all five independent acceptance groups.

The preservation review still asked for the entire patch a second time: it treated a changed fs.lstatSync argument as a missing call. This round used 25% less input than native Codex but took longer. The following round tests the narrower preservation check.

Native Astra completed the same extension and retained tests in six model requests. It passed all five independent acceptance groups. This fresh native run accompanies the factory’s batch-edit revision.

Astra reviewed Terra’s implementation and commissioned stricter hash validation, raw root-path handling, and missing behavioral tests. It corrected a generated fixture that normalized away the very path component it was meant to test.

A later review caught an overrestriction: the selected root cannot be a symlink, but its ancestors may be. Terra repaired that distinction and retained positive and negative cases. All five independent acceptance groups passed; the full token total counts every supervisor and worker call.

explanation.title: Correct the fixture. Check the boundary.

paragraphs.text: Astra steered Sol through an incorrect test expectation: a regular file used as an intermediate path component belongs in unsafe. The correction retained the case and its assertion.

Review then caught root normalization stripping a literal POSIX backslash. Sol repaired that boundary and added regressions, isolated size-only drift, and used a read spy to check that complete manifest validation precedes file reads. Astra reviewed the integrated result; all five independent acceptance groups passed.
